summary.text: Dometic WH-series RV tank water heaters (WH-6GA, WH-6GEA, WH-9GEA, WH-10GEA, WH-16GEA) heat with LP gas through direct spark ignition and, on GEA models, a 110 VAC element. Faults show as a lockout: if the gas fails to light after three attempts the red lockout lamp illuminates, and an E.C.O. trip also locks the heater out until reset.

models.text: The 2022 manual covers WH-6GA (6 gal gas), WH-6GEA (6 gal gas/electric), WH-9GEA (9 gal effective), WH-10GEA (10 gal gas/electric) and WH-16GEA (16 gal effective).
Model code WH-6GEA: WH = water heater, number = gallons, G = gas (propane), E = electric AC element, A = revision; the instructions apply regardless of revision number.
9GEA and 16GEA are effective sizes: the tanks hold 6 and 10 gallons, and a mixing valve delivers 9 or 16 gallons of 130°F (54°C) moderated water.
XT models G9EXT, GE9EXT, GEH9EXT, G16EXT, GE16EXT and GEH16EXT: G = gas, E = electric, H = engine heat exchanger, EXT = Electronic Exothermal (XT) technology.
Gas pressure must be 10 to 13 in. W.C.; the 12 V supply must be 10 to 14 VDC.
Dometic and Atwood brand water heater tanks are high-strength aluminum and do not use anode rods.
The OD-5001 on-demand heater stays dormant until a tap is opened and it senses water flow of at least 1.0 GPM.
models.locator: support page 'How to operate your water heater', step 4

display.text: Gas mode: when switched ON the heater makes three attempts to light; if there is no ignition it locks out and the red lockout lamp illuminates.
The wall switch light stays on during ignition and goes out once the control detects flame; if ignition fails the red lockout lamp stays illuminated.
Gas and electric together: a gas lockout does not light the lamp while electric is running; slow recovery is the sign. Switch electric OFF and the lamp lights if gas is locked out.
If the water gets too hot the heater goes into a lockout condition with the indicator light on.
Burner obstruction signs: a change in burner sound, or the flame changing from hard blue to soft and lazy or very yellow; nests cause poor combustion and delayed ignition.
A P/T relief valve dripping while the heater runs does not mean it is defective; heated water expands and slowly absorbs the tank's internal air gap.

reset.text: Gas lockout: determine and correct the cause, then reset the gas control by turning the switch OFF, then ON.
If the control switch light stays on longer than 15 seconds, place the switch OFF, wait 5 minutes, and repeat.
Electric E.C.O. lockout: check the thermostat has good contact with the tank, then turn the electric switch OFF, then ON.
Overheat lockout: find and correct the cause, let the water cool, place the control switch OFF for 30 seconds, then ON.
Dometic support notes the water can take up to 30 minutes to cool before the overheat reset.
reset.locator: support page 'How to clear a water heater over-heating failure'

reset.text: OD-5001: if the heater fails to light or the optional lockout lamp lights, turn the power switch OFF, then ON; first use may need several water on/off cycles to purge air from LP lines.
reset.locator: support page 'How to operate your water heater', step 5

checks.text: Never operate the heater without water in the tank.
If unused for more than two weeks, open the kitchen hot faucet for several minutes before using electrical appliances on the hot water system; hydrogen gas may have formed.
Keep the vent and combustion air grill clear, and periodically check the main burner flame.
Inspect for and remove dust and insect nests from the burner compartment and flue assembly.
Electrical checks: low voltage below 10 VDC on the thermostat line; if the board fuse is good and the unit is dead, excessively high voltage over 14 volts.
Drain the heater at least once a year and before winter storage or freezing; about two quarts stay in the tank and will not cause freeze damage.
Flush the tank every 60 days for full-time RVers (30 in the Southwest) and at least twice a year part-time (every 90 days in the Southwest).
Turn gas off at the LP tank while the vehicle is moving and shut off gas appliances when refueling.

parts.text: Named components: access door, tank, flue assembly, hot outlet, cold inlet, gas valve, electrode, E.C.O./thermostat, thermal cut-off, P/T relief valve, DSI control board and electric junction box/element.
DSI control board carries a 2 amp mini ATO fuse against wiring shorts; if it blows the heater will not operate. Never install a fuse larger than 3 amps.
Thermal cut-off in the power supply line melts if flame or heat reaches it, for example from a flue obstruction; the obstruction must be removed and the cut-off replaced.
Ignition electrode: porcelain must not be cracked and the electrode-to-ground gap is 0.125 in. (1/8 in.).
EXT/XT mixing valve moderates outlet water to about 130°F (54°C); it is not serviceable and must be replaced only by a certified technician.
P/T relief valve is not serviceable; a replacement must be a combination P/T valve certified to ANSI Z21.22 with set pressure not over 150 psi.
Do not use anode rods, bug screens or aftermarket heating elements; aftermarket elements can lack critical safety controls and lead to tank explosion, and any alteration voids the warranty.

callTech.text: If you smell gas: evacuate everyone, shut off gas at the container, touch no electrical switch, phone or radio, do not start the engine or generator, and call a gas supplier, qualified technician or fire department.
Do not turn the gas supply back on until the leak is repaired; installation and service must be done by a qualified installer, service agency or gas supplier.
Overheating, or gas that fails to shut off: turn the operating switch OFF and remove the red wire from the E.C.O. left terminal, or turn the gas off at the LP tank.
If the lockout persists after the reset, read the maintenance instructions and contact a Dometic Service Center.
EXT models with low hot-water flow or water not as hot: the mixing valve may be faulty from corrosion or debris; call a technician for repair.
Have the gas pressure tested periodically; it should be 11 in. water column with three appliances running.
Insect nests in the burner or flue that cannot be easily removed: contact a qualified service center.
